llm.summary: This HubSpot skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but its setup instructions include unverified remote installer commands that can execute changing code on a user's machine.

dimensions.detail: The declared tool permission is limited to Bash(oo *), and credentials are described as injected server-side, but the skill can access and modify business CRM data once the connected account is authorized.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup tells users to run curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex installers from remote URLs without pinning, checksum/signature verification, or an explicit review step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language covers any HubSpot request, which is broad, but the runtime workflow is otherwise scoped to HubSpot connector schema and run commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, background worker, memory poisoning, or hidden persistence is present in the artifact; one-time CLI install and OOMOL login may create ordinary local tooling or auth state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill coherently targets HubSpot CRM read and write operations through OOMOL's oo CLI, with write actions labeled and user confirmation required before state-changing calls.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the setup path before installing. The HubSpot actions and write confirmations are reasonably disclosed, but avoid running the remote installer pipelines unless you trust OOMOL's installer delivery path; prefer a versioned installer, documented checksum/signature verification, or official package manager flow where available.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: The installer is related to enabling the oo CLI, but the artifact-backed curl-to-bash instruction is a real supply-chain concern because it immediately executes mutable remote code.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad HubSpot trigger language matches a HubSpot integration skill, but users should understand it may activate for many HubSpot-related requests.
[T03] expected: The remote Bash and PowerShell installer commands are purpose-related setup steps, not evidence of malicious intent, but they justify Review because they lack verification and could run arbitrary code if the remote installer path is compromised.
